objectives.text: Keep Emmerson Mnangagwa in office to 2030. The Senate passed a constitutional amendment on 24 June 2026 by 75 votes to 4, lengthening presidential terms from five to seven years, ending direct election of the president (parliament elects him) and keeping him in office until 2030. The bill still needed his signature in the source read; the signature date is not verified.

objectives.text: Turn lithium and other raw minerals into processing income at home. Harare suspended exports of raw minerals and lithium concentrate in February 2026 to push local processing, and officials say the policy drew more than USD 1bn into the lithium value chain. means.text: Lithium and gold. Zimbabwe exported 1.128 million tonnes of lithium-bearing spodumene concentrate in the year to December 2025, up 11% on the year before, most of it to China for processing into battery materials. The raw-material export ban (February 2026) is the state's lever over that flow.

constraints.text: A single buyer for the mineral chain. Most of Zimbabwe's lithium output goes to China and Chinese firms own the largest mines, so Beijing's processors set the terms of the value chain the export ban is meant to build. The 2022 USD 180m purchase of Bikita Minerals by Sinomine is the best-known case.

paradoxes.text: The export ban meant to keep value at home favours the Chinese-financed plants that can afford processing. A Bikita community leader sees no tangible jobs from value addition, and smaller miners warn that processing plants, unreliable power and scarce finance keep them out, so the policy meant to widen the base may concentrate it.

sources.title: Can Zimbabwe's mineral ambitions benefit smaller producers?

grand_strategy.reading: Zimbabwe's grand strategy is the survival of the ZANU-PF system under Mnangagwa: the 2026 amendment extends his rule to 2030 by moving the choice of president from voters to parliament. Its money comes from minerals, above all lithium, that flow mostly to China, which funds and buys the extraction, while the Western sanctions that remain (the 2024 Global Magnitsky listings and ZIDERA) keep the other door narrow. The export ban is the state's attempt to turn that dependence into domestic value, and the paradox is that the Chinese-financed plants are the ones best placed to benefit from it.

stances.note: Chinese capital runs Zimbabwe's lithium: Chinese firms (Sinomine, Huayou, Chengxin, Yahua) drive the spodumene build-up, and Sinomine bought Bikita Minerals for USD 180m in February 2022 (search results, article not opened). Most output goes to China. Partner is our reading of transactional cooperation without alignment (C): no source in this pass uses the word, and no treaty or defence clause was found. stances_toward.note: Partner, stable. The fourth session of the Bi-National Commission (set up in April 2015) met in Pretoria on 21 August 2026 and signed agreements on diplomacy, correctional services, gender, agriculture and arts and heritage, with a business forum the same day; Ramaphosa called Zimbabwe one of South Africa's largest trading partners (SAnews). South African goods exports to Zimbabwe were about USD 4.3bn in 2025 (UN Comtrade via Trading Economics, tier 4). Migration is the sore point: the Zimbabwean Exemption Permit was extended to 28 May 2027 by the Home Affairs minister's directive of October 2025 with no permanent solution found, and Ramaphosa's emergency private visit to Zimbabwe in early 2026 was questioned by the DA (search coverage; page not opened). Mnangagwa was SADC chair before South Africa. The ANC-ZANU-PF liberation tie is not read in the sources, so bond none is our reading.
